ccsTitle: Leg Pain - Emergency Medicine / Internal Medicine
diagnosis: Cellulitis (bacterial skin/soft tissue infection of the calf) in poorly controlled type 2 diabetes

patient.key: Poorly demarcated warm erythematous indurated anterior calf + fever/leukocytosis in uncontrolled DM2; duplex ruled out DVT

sequence.what: Fever 38.3 C, otherwise stable vitals; BMI 27
sequence.decision: Systemic infection signal already present before you examine the leg

sequence.what: 50M DM2 with week of progressive left leg swelling, heat, redness, pain worse with walking, better with elevation; no trauma
sequence.decision: Unilateral inflammatory leg + diabetes = soft tissue infection until proven otherwise; still must exclude DVT

sequence.what: Poorly demarcated diffusely erythematous indurated anterior calf; no ulcer, drainage, or purulence; HEENT/chest/heart normal
sequence.decision: Classic non-purulent cellulitis geometry — not abscess, not nec fasc demarcation

sequence.what: CBC WBC 11.3k; venous duplex: no DVT; CMP ordered; blood cultures ordered; metformin continued
sequence.decision: Leukocytosis + negative duplex clears the major mimic and supports bacterial soft tissue infection

sequence.what: Clindamycin IM, LR IV, stayed in ED; missed insulin, analgesia, A1c, UA, diabetes teaching, Tdap, inpatient transfer
sequence.decision: Systemic signs need IV abx on the floor plus glucose control and pain — ED boarding is the wrong destination

missed.why: In a febrile diabetic with soft tissue infection, UA screens for concurrent UTI/bacteruria that can seed or amplify bacteremia and explain persistent fever after the leg is treated.

This cellulitis is a complication of chronic hyperglycemia. A1c proves the months-long glucose failure that impairs neutrophil chemotaxis and skin barrier healing — it is the disease that invited the bug.
He cannot walk on a hot swollen calf and took nothing at home. Pain control is part of treating soft tissue infection, not optional comfort.
Infection drives stress hyperglycemia; metformin alone will not correct the acute glucose that further cripples leukocyte function. Score explicitly wanted insulin and metformin stopped.
Without teaching on glucose monitoring, foot/skin care, and adherence, he returns with the next portal of entry cellulitis. Preventive care scored 0%.
No recent vaccinations documented; soft tissue infection workup is a catch-up vaccination moment every 10 years.
Fever + leukocytosis cellulitis needs inpatient IV antibiotics. Staying in the ED at 00:15 and 15:15 sim time was graded wrong location.

correctHighlights: Exam: general, skin, extremities, chest, heart, abdomen

mechanismsForImage.title: Diabetic skin barrier

mechanismsForImage.title: Bacterial entry
mechanismsForImage.concept: Gram-positive organisms invade dermis/subcutis through microbreaches

mechanismsForImage.title: Spreading cellulitis
mechanismsForImage.concept: Poorly demarcated erythema, warmth, edema expand through soft tissue planes

mechanismsForImage.title: Systemic response
mechanismsForImage.concept: Fever and leukocytosis as cytokine response to soft tissue infection

mechanismsForImage.title: Rule out DVT
mechanismsForImage.concept: Venous duplex clears clot mimic of unilateral swollen red leg

mechanismsForImage.title: Empiric IV antibiotics
mechanismsForImage.concept: Gram-positive coverage floods infected tissue planes

mechanismsForImage.title: Insulin and glucose
mechanismsForImage.concept: Insulin restores leukocyte function while metformin-only fails under stress
